title: Case Studies and the 2026 State of the Art

questions.question: A research task has independent questions, needs fresh worker contexts, and requires one lead to synthesize the findings. Which case study is the closest reference?
options: Anthropic Research's supervisor-worker pattern
A flat queue with no coordinating agent
MetaGPT's SOP-encoded engineering roles
OpenClaw's population-scale social substrate
questions.explanation: Anthropic Research is the supervisor-worker reference: a lead decomposes independent questions, subagents work in focused contexts, and the lead synthesizes results. MetaGPT’s SOP roles target a structured engineering process rather than broad parallel research.

questions.question: A software project encodes its process in distinct product, architecture, engineering, and QA roles with structured handoffs. Which case study fits?
options: OpenClaw and Moltbook
Anthropic Research
MetaGPT and ChatDev
A consensus-only voting ensemble
questions.explanation: MetaGPT and ChatDev encode software SOPs in distinct roles and pass structured artifacts between them. OpenClaw/Moltbook illustrates a population-scale social substrate, not the product-architect-engineer-QA workflow in the scenario.

questions.question: A network lets many independently operated agents publish profiles and exchange messages. Which security assumption from the case studies should apply?
options: Assume population-scale traffic removes prompt injection
Trust every profile because it was written by an agent
Allow all agents to share production credentials
Treat agent profiles and cross-agent messages as untrusted input
questions.explanation: Profiles and cross-agent messages are untrusted input because a malicious instruction can propagate through many agent interactions. Trusting every profile simply because an agent authored it removes the boundary that the case study says to enforce.

questions.question: A research agent may run for hours while a new runtime version is deployed. Which case-study practice supports this workload?
options: Sending every task through a single synchronous call
Rainbow deployment that lets older runs drain
Removing checkpoints before deploying new code
Restarting every agent on the newest version immediately
questions.explanation: Rainbow deployment keeps old runtime versions alive until long-running agents finish, while new work can move to a new version. Restarting every agent immediately can interrupt in-flight stateful work during the deploy.

questions.question: Across the three case studies, which production pattern appears as a common requirement?
options: Structured handoffs and independent verification
One universal topology for every task type
More agents without role or task boundaries
A single final transcript without intermediate traces
questions.explanation: The cases converge on structured handoff contracts and independent verification, while their topologies vary with the task. One universal topology would ignore those differences rather than transfer a common engineering practice.

questions.question: A team is adapting a multi-agent case study for a public service where agents can message one another. Which review should happen before launch?
options: Copy the published agent count and keep every default unchanged
Check trust boundaries, verification, cost, and population-scale security
Optimize only raw benchmark accuracy and omit cost reports
Remove handoff logs so profiles cannot be audited
questions.explanation: For a public cross-agent service, review trust boundaries, independent verification, cost, and population-scale security before launch. Copying a case study’s agent count and defaults does not test whether its assumptions fit this service.
